gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold specifies a 3‑day history of dysuria AND suprapubic pain. Generated HPI mentions a several‑day history of dysuria but does not state the 3‑day duration and does not identify suprapubic location; ROS lower abdominal pain also lacks duration and exact site. Therefore the full gold fact (3 days + suprapubic) is not fully captured.
Gold: patient denies urinary frequency. Generated HPI‑005 explicitly states patient denies increased urinary frequency.

Gold: brief episode of hematuria now resolved. Generated notes one small amount of blood in urine earlier today but does not state it has resolved. The resolution component is missing, so the gold fact is not fully captured.
Gold: urine is foul‑smelling. Generated HPI‑004/ROS‑004: urine has an unusual/abnormal malodorous smell. Semantically equivalent.

Gold: abdominal pain is cramping and non‑radiating. Generated HPI‑002 describes crampy lower abdominal pain distinct from menstrual cramps, but does not state that the pain does not radiate. The non‑radiating aspect is omitted.

Gold: denies nausea, vomiting, fever, AND bowel symptoms. Generated HPI‑009/010/011 cover denial of nausea, vomiting, fevers. Bowel symptoms are not explicitly denied in HPI; HPI‑007 only says no change in bowel habits (not equivalent to no bowel symptoms). Thus the full gold fact is not completely covered.

Gold: sexually active with a regular partner for the past 2 months. Generated SH‑005: sexually active with one regular partner and uses condoms; timing (2 months) is not mentioned. Duration component is omitted.
Gold: no previous STD screening. Generated HPI‑015: no prior STD screening. Direct match.
Gold: patient denies vaginal discharge. Generated HPI‑013 and ROS‑008: no vaginal / no abnormal vaginal discharge. Effectively the same denial.
Gold: LMP 2 weeks ago. Generated HPI‑014: LMP approximately three weeks ago. This is a different timing, so the gold fact (2 weeks) is not correctly captured.
Gold: history of IBS. Generated PMH‑001: patient has history of irritable bowel syndrome. Directly matches.
Gold: no regular medications. Generated MED‑002: patient takes no regular medications. Direct match.
Gold: allergic to clindamycin. Generated ALLERGY‑001: allergic to clindamycin causing swelling. The basic allergy is covered; generated adds reaction detail.

Gold: no relevant family history (general). Generated FHX‑001: no known family history of kidney, bladder, bowel, or GI problems (specific organ systems). This is more specific and does not explicitly state that there is no other relevant family history; thus it does not fully capture the broader gold statement.
Gold: patient is 19 years old. No age is documented in the generated facts.
Gold: student studying Biology and lives in a flat with friends. Generated SH‑001 and SH‑002: lives in a flat near college with friends; biology student. Both elements are present.
Gold: non‑smoker and social alcohol at weekends. Generated SH‑003 and SH‑004: does not smoke; social alcohol use on weekends. Direct match.

Gold: impression is UTI/cystitis. Generated ASM‑001: likely uncomplicated urinary tract infection. This conveys the same primary impression; cystitis is a form of lower UTI and is reasonably encompassed.

Gold: 3‑day course of either Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim. Generated PLAN‑001: empiric oral Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, one tablet twice daily for three days. The 3‑day antibiotic course is covered (with added dosing detail).

Gold: advised to increase fluids and try cranberry juice. Generated PLAN‑002 and PLAN‑003: encourage increased fluid intake; cranberry juice recommended as optional symptom relief. Both interventions are captured.
Gold: advised to avoid having sex. Generated PLAN‑005: avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve and continue barrier contraception. The avoidance advice is covered (with extra detail).

Gold: pregnancy test will be performed to exclude pregnancy. Generated PLAN‑007: advise pregnancy test if any suspicion arises. This changes from a planned test to a contingent recommendation, so it does not capture the definite plan in the gold fact.
Gold: review in 3 days if not better. Generated FU‑001: contact clinic if not improved by the end of the week. Timing (3 days vs end of week) is different; thus not covered.

Gold: seek earlier review for worsening symptoms such as fevers, back pain, vomiting, or feeling more unwell. Generated PLAN‑006 and FU‑001: advise prompt attention if fever, worsening/back pain, or feeling unwell develop. Vomiting is not explicitly repeated but ‘worsening pain/feeling unwell’ plus fever/back pain match the listed examples closely; the essence of the gold follow‑up warning is captured.
